content_pages|allergies|summary: What we can and cannot do for passengers with food allergies.
content_pages|allergies|body_html:
We cannot guarantee an allergen-free cabin

Our aircraft are not free of nuts, dairy, gluten, sesame or shellfish. Other passengers may bring food on board, and cabins are not deep-cleaned between every sector. We therefore cannot describe any flight as allergen-free.

Before you travel

  • Tell us at least 48 hours before departure by adding a note to your booking or calling the contact office for your country.
  • Order a special meal that excludes your allergen. Special meals close 24 hours before departure and cannot be arranged at the airport.
  • Carry your own antihistamines and adrenaline auto-injector in your cabin baggage, not in the hold. Cabin crew carry a medical kit but it is not a substitute for your own medication.
  • Bring a doctor's letter if you carry injectable medication, so it is not questioned at security.

On board

Tell the cabin crew when you board. They can make an announcement asking other passengers not to open nut products, and they will note your seat. The announcement is a request, not an enforceable rule.

You may bring your own sealed food on board for your own consumption.

Buffer zones

On request we will seat you away from the galley and note a buffer of one row in front and behind. Buffer zones cannot be guaranteed on a full flight.
content_pages|special-baggage|summary: Rules, weight limits and charges for sports equipment and outsize items.
content_pages|special-baggage|body_html:
How special baggage is charged

Sports equipment counts as one checked bag if it is within your free allowance and under the weight limit for the item. Anything above that is charged at the fixed item fee below, which replaces the normal excess-weight rate.

Items marked as requiring advance notice must be declared at least 48 hours before departure. We cannot accept them at the airport without a booking.

Packing requirements

  • Bicycles must have the handlebars turned, pedals removed and tyres deflated, in a bicycle bag or box.
  • Firearms for sport require a permit and must be declared; ammunition is limited to 5 kg per passenger and must travel separately from the firearm.
  • Surfboards and windsurf equipment must be in a padded board bag.
  • Diving cylinders must be empty, with the valve removed or open for inspection.

Items we cannot carry

Loose lithium batteries above 160 Wh, powered ride-on suitcases with non-removable batteries, and hoverboards are not accepted in either cabin or hold baggage on any route.
content_pages|cabin-baggage|summary: Size, weight and what must go in the hold instead.
content_pages|cabin-baggage|body_html:
What you may carry into the cabin

One cabin bag of up to 7 kg in Selam Economy and 14 kg in Highland Class, not exceeding 55 x 38 x 20 cm including wheels and handles. One personal item such as a handbag or laptop bag may be carried in addition.

On full flights and on Dash 8-400 services, cabin bags may be placed in the hold at the gate at no charge. Remove medication, documents and valuables first.

Liquids

Containers of up to 100 ml each, in a single transparent resealable bag of no more than one litre. Baby food and prescribed medication for the journey are exempt but must be declared at security.
content_pages|baggage-infants|summary: Allowances for passengers under 12, and what counts as equipment.
content_pages|baggage-infants|body_html:
Infants under two

An infant travelling on an adult's lap has one checked bag of up to 10 kg and no cabin baggage allowance of their own.

One pushchair and one car seat travel free on every route, in addition to the allowance, and may be taken to the aircraft door.

Children aged two to eleven

A child with their own seat has the same free allowance as an adult on the same route and cabin.
content_pages|baggage-codeshare|summary: Whose rules apply when part of your journey is flown by another airline.
content_pages|baggage-codeshare|body_htm:
The first marketing carrier sets the allowance

Where a journey booked with us includes a sector operated by a partner, our allowance applies throughout, provided the whole journey is on one booking reference. Separate bookings are treated as separate journeys and each carrier's own rules apply.

Partner-operated sectors cannot be checked in online; use the airport desk.
content_pages|baggage-restricted|summary: What may not travel at all, and what may travel only in the hold.
content_pages|baggage-restricted|body_ht:
Never accepted

  • Explosives, fireworks and flares.
  • Compressed gases, including camping gas and unapproved oxygen cylinders.
  • Corrosives such as mercury, wet-cell batteries and drain cleaner.

Hold only

Sharp articles, tools longer than 6 cm, sporting bats and cricket stumps must be checked. Spare lithium batteries are the reverse: they must travel in the cabin and never in the hold.
content_pages|airport-checkin|summary: Desk opening and closing times, and when you must use a desk.
content_pages|airport-checkin|body_html:
Desk times

Desks open 3 hours before an international departure and 2 hours before a domestic one, and close 60 minutes before departure on all routes. Bag drop for passengers already checked in online closes at the same time.

When a desk is required

Passengers travelling with an infant on the lap, an unaccompanied minor, booked special assistance, or on a partner-operated sector must check in at a desk. Group bookings of ten or more are handled by the group desk.
content_pages|boarding-and-gates|summary: When boarding starts, and what happens if you arrive late at the gate.
content_pages|boarding-and-gates|body_ht:
Timings

Boarding begins 40 minutes before departure and the gate closes 20 minutes before. A boarding pass shows the boarding time, not the departure time, in its boarding field.

Passengers not at the gate at closure are offloaded with their baggage and the fare rules of their ticket determine whether a rebooking is chargeable.
content_pages|fare-rules-explained|summa: What each fare family allows, and where to find the rules for your own ticket.
content_pages|fare-rules-explained|body_:
Fare families

Promo and Lite fares are neither refundable nor changeable. Basic and Group fares may be changed for a fee but are not refundable. Standard is half refundable. Flex is fully refundable and changes are free. Highland Class fares are refundable in full, with a fee on the Saver family only.

The fare family of your own ticket is shown beside each flight when you open your booking, as a two-letter code such as EF or HC.
content_pages|involuntary-changes|title: If we change or cancel your flight
content_pages|involuntary-changes|summar: Your options when the change is ours rather than yours.
content_pages|involuntary-changes|body_h:
Rebooking and refunds

Where we cancel a flight or reschedule it by more than three hours, you may take the next available flight at no charge, or request a full refund regardless of the fare rules of your ticket. This is separate from a voluntary change and no change fee or fare difference applies.

Requests under this policy are handled by the contact office for your country, not by the online refund form.
content_pages|special-meals|summary: The meal codes we carry and when they must be ordered.
content_pages|special-meals|body_html:
Ordering

Special meals must be requested at least 24 hours before departure through your booking. They cannot be arranged at the airport or on board, and a request made inside the cut-off will not be loaded.

A special meal is prepared to a dietary specification. It is not an allergy control: it reduces but does not remove the risk of cross-contact, and the cabin itself is not allergen-free.

Codes we carry

  • VGML vegetarian, VJML Jain vegetarian, AVML Asian vegetarian.
  • GFML gluten intolerant, LFML low fat, LSML low salt, DBML diabetic.
  • HNML Hindu, MOML Muslim, KSML kosher, ORML Orthodox fasting.
  • CHML child, BBML infant, FPML fruit platter.
content_pages|medical-conditions|summary: When we need medical clearance, and what to bring.
content_pages|medical-conditions|body_ht:
Clearance

Medical clearance is required within 7 days of surgery, for conditions needing supplementary oxygen, for a pregnancy beyond 36 weeks, and where a stretcher or medical escort is needed. Apply at least 72 hours before departure.

Carry prescribed medication in your cabin baggage in its original labelled packaging, with a doctor's letter for anything injectable.
content_pages|assistance-mobility|summar: Wheelchair codes, and how a request changes your check-in.
content_pages|assistance-mobility|body_h:
Codes

WCHR means assistance to the aircraft door with the passenger able to climb steps; WCHS means unable to climb steps; WCHC means immobile throughout and requiring assistance to the seat. Request at least 48 hours ahead.

A booking with assistance recorded cannot be checked in online; a desk agent must confirm the arrangements in person.
content_pages|miles-earning|summary: Earning rates by fare family, and what does not earn.
content_pages|miles-earning|body_html:
Rates

Miles are earned as a percentage of distance flown, set by fare family: Promo earns nothing, Lite 25%, Basic 50%, Group 75%, Standard 100%, Flex 125%. Highland Class earns 150% to 250% depending on family.

Award tickets, staff tickets and the taxes portion of any fare do not earn miles. Miles credit within 72 hours of travel; after that, claim them.
content_pages|miles-tiers|summary: Thresholds, benefits and how status is retained.
content_pages|miles-tiers|body_html:
Thresholds

Blue is the entry tier. Silver requires 25,000 qualifying miles in a membership year, Gold 50,000, and Platinum 100,000. Qualifying miles are distance-based and differ from the redeemable miles shown as your balance.

Gold and Platinum members and Highland Class passengers have lounge access; Silver does not.
content_pages|miles-expiry|summary: How long miles last and what keeps an account active.
content_pages|miles-expiry|body_html:
Validity

Redeemable miles are valid for 36 months from the month they are credited. Any earning or redemption activity extends the whole balance by a further 36 months. An account with no activity for 24 months is made dormant and must be reactivated before miles can be used.
content_pages|wifi-and-power|summary: Which aircraft have sockets, and how connectivity differs by type.
content_pages|wifi-and-power|body_html:
Power

Boeing 787-8 and Airbus A350-900 aircraft have a universal socket at every seat and USB at every seat. Boeing 737-800 and A320neo have USB only. Dash 8-400 and Embraer 175 have neither.

Connectivity is available only on Wi-Fi-equipped aircraft. Whether your own flight is equipped is shown on the flight status page for that flight.
content_pages|entertainment|summary: What is available, and on which aircraft.
content_pages|entertainment|body_html:
Seat-back and streaming

Wide-body aircraft have seat-back screens with roughly 200 films, 60 series and a music library. Narrow-body aircraft stream the same library to your own device over the on-board network, which does not require a Wi-Fi package.
content_pages|travel-documents|summary: Validity rules and the checks we make at the airport.
content_pages|travel-documents|body_html:
Validity

Most destinations require a passport valid for at least six months beyond your date of arrival, with at least two blank pages. It is the passenger's responsibility to hold the correct documents; we are required to refuse carriage where they are not in order.
content_pages|visa-transit|summary: When a transit passenger needs a visa, and when they do not.
content_pages|visa-transit|body_html:
Airside transit

A passenger connecting within the same terminal on a single booking generally does not need a transit visa. A visa is needed where the connection requires leaving the transit area, where baggage must be reclaimed and re-checked, or where the layover is long enough that you intend to leave the airport.
content_pages|restricted-items-full|summ: The full list, by category, with where each may travel.
content_pages|restricted-items-full|body:
Batteries and powered devices

Spare lithium batteries up to 100 Wh travel in the cabin only, with terminals taped. Between 100 and 160 Wh you may carry two, with prior approval. Above 160 Wh we cannot carry them at all.

Powered wheelchairs are carried, but the battery type must be declared at least 48 hours ahead so the right handling is arranged.

Liquids, aerosols and gels

In the cabin: containers of up to 100 ml, in one transparent bag of up to one litre. In the hold: up to 2 litres of any single item and 2 kg in total, for toiletries and medicines only.

Sharp and pointed articles

Scissors with blades under 6 cm are allowed in the cabin. Anything longer, and all knives, tools and needles other than medical ones, must be checked.
content_pages|musical-instruments|summar: Which instruments travel in the cabin, which need a seat, and which go in the hold.
content_pages|musical-instruments|body_h:
In the cabin

An instrument within the cabin baggage dimensions -- 55 x 38 x 20 cm -- counts as your cabin bag. Violins and flutes normally qualify; guitars do not.

On an extra seat

Instruments up to 80 kg and 165 cm may travel on a seat bought for them, at the adult fare for the cabin, booked at least 72 hours ahead. The instrument must be in a hard case and is secured by the crew.

In the hold

Larger instruments travel as checked baggage in a hard flight case, at the special-baggage rate. We do not accept liability for instruments carried in the hold in a soft case.
content_pages|fitness-to-fly|summary: When you may travel without clearance, and when you may not travel at all.
content_pages|fitness-to-fly|body_html:
Pregnancy

You may travel without a letter up to the end of the 28th week. From 29 to 36 weeks bring a letter from a doctor or midwife dated within 10 days of travel. After 36 weeks -- 32 for a multiple pregnancy -- we cannot carry you.

After surgery or illness

Wait 24 hours after keyhole surgery and 10 days after chest or abdominal surgery. After a heart attack, wait 7 days if recovery was uncomplicated. Medical clearance is required inside these periods.

Infants

Infants may fly from seven days old. Below that we carry them only with a neonatal letter.
content_pages|unaccompanied-minors|summa: Age bands, the escort service, and what must be arranged before travel.
content_pages|unaccompanied-minors|body_:
Age bands

Under 5 may not travel alone. From 5 to 11 the escort service is compulsory and costs USD 60 each way. From 12 to 15 it is optional at the same price. From 16 the passenger travels as an adult.

Before travel

Book at least 48 hours ahead and name the adult handing over and the adult collecting, with a telephone number for each. Both must bring photographic identification. A booking with an unaccompanied minor cannot be checked in online.
content_pages|travelling-with-pets|summa: Cabin and hold rules, weight limits, and the documents each destination needs.
content_pages|travelling-with-pets|body_:
In the cabin

Cats and dogs up to 8 kg including the carrier may travel in the cabin, at USD 90 per sector. The carrier must fit under the seat in front, and only one animal per passenger is accepted.

In the hold

Above 8 kg the animal travels in the hold in an IATA-compliant crate, at USD 200 per sector. We do not carry snub-nosed breeds in the hold on any route, because they cannot regulate their breathing reliably.

Documents

Every destination sets its own import rules. A rabies vaccination certificate and an export health certificate are the minimum; some destinations add a titre test with a waiting period of several months. Check before you book.
content_pages|corporate-programme|summar: What the programme offers, and the threshold to join it.
content_pages|corporate-programme|body_h:
What members get

Negotiated fares on the routes you fly most, consolidated monthly billing, waived change fees on Standard and above, and a named account manager.

Joining

Programmes start from USD 50,000 of annual travel spend. Below that, book through the website and earn Selam Miles in the usual way.
content_pages|changing-a-booking|summary: What can be changed, what it costs, and what cannot be changed at all.
content_pages|changing-a-booking|body_ht:
What a change covers

A change moves you to a different date, a different flight on the same route, or a different route. It never changes who is travelling: a new passenger needs a new booking, whatever the fare.

What it costs

Two amounts are involved and they are separate. The change fee is set by your fare class and is waived on some fares. The fare difference is the gap between what you paid and the price of the new flight on the day you change it, and no fare waives it.

If the new flight is cheaper, the difference is not refunded. It stays as a credit against a further change on the same booking.

What cannot be changed

  • A flight that has already departed. Once a segment is flown or missed, the rest of the booking follows the no-show rules instead.
  • An award ticket within 72 hours of departure.
  • A booking made through a travel agent, which the agent must change.
content_pages|cancelling-and-refunds|sum: Cancelling and refunding are two decisions, not one.
content_pages|cancelling-and-refunds|bod:
They are not the same thing

Cancelling releases your seats. Refunding returns money. Cancelling does not trigger a refund, and on a non-refundable fare it returns nothing at all -- so cancel only after you have seen what the refund rules give you.

What each fare returns

  • Flex fares refund in full, less a processing fee.
  • Standard fares refund a percentage, set by the fare rules on your booking.
  • Saver and promotional fares refund the government taxes only. The base fare is not returned.

How long it takes

Approved refunds reach the original payment method in 7 to 21 working days. Bookings made through an agent are refunded to the agent, not to you.
content_pages|name-corrections|summary: Which spelling mistakes we can fix, and which need a new ticket.
content_pages|name-corrections|body_html:
Corrections we make free of charge

  • Up to three letters in a first or last name, where the name is clearly the same person -- a transposed pair, a missing letter, an accented character dropped.
  • Reversed first and last name.
  • Adding or removing a middle name to match the passport.

What needs a new booking

A different person, a legal name change, or a correction of more than three letters. A ticket is not transferable, so this is a cancellation under your fare rules followed by a fresh purchase.

Bring the correction to us before check-in opens. After a boarding pass is issued the name is fixed and the airport cannot change it.
content_pages|payment-methods|summary: Cards, bank transfer, vouchers and miles, and when each is available.
content_pages|payment-methods|body_html:
Accepted methods

  • Major credit and debit cards, in USD.
  • Bank transfer, for bookings made more than 14 days before departure. The booking is held for 72 hours while the transfer clears.
  • Gift vouchers, in part or in full, against the base fare.
  • Selam Miles, for award tickets and for upgrades.

What we do not accept

Cash at the airport for a web booking, cheques, and payment by a third party whose name is not on the booking. Taxes and carrier charges cannot be paid in vouchers.
content_pages|online-checkin-guide|summa: The window, what you need, and the eight reasons it can refuse you.
content_pages|online-checkin-guide|body_:
The window

Check-in opens 48 hours before departure and closes 2 hours before. Outside that window the page will tell you which of the two applies; it does not queue your request for later.

When it will refuse

Eight conditions stop online check-in, and each shows its own message rather than a generic failure: too early, closed, an infant on a lap, special assistance booked, an unaccompanied minor, a document check we must do in person, a flight operated by a partner airline, and a group booking.

In every one of those cases you check in at the airport instead, and the desk closes at the same time as online check-in.
content_pages|seat-choice-explained|summ: Window, aisle, bulkhead, exit row and bassinet, and who may sit where.
content_pages|seat-choice-explained|body:
The markings

  • Window: against the cabin wall, with no direct access to the aisle.
  • Aisle: beside the aisle, the easiest seat to leave the row from.
  • Bulkhead: the first row of a cabin. More legroom, but nothing in front to store a bag under, so everything goes in the overhead locker for take-off.
  • Exit row: extra legroom, and a duty to help the crew in an evacuation.
  • Bassinet: a bassinet can be fitted, so these are held for passengers with an infant.

Who may not sit in an exit row

Passengers under 15, passengers travelling with an infant, passengers who need an extension seatbelt, and anyone who would find it hard to operate a heavy door. Cabin crew reseat anyone who does not qualify, and the seat charge is refunded.
content_pages|waitlist-and-standby|summa: How a waitlist clears, and how standby differs from it.
content_pages|waitlist-and-standby|body_:
Waitlist

A waitlist holds you for a fare class that is sold out on a flight you have already booked. It clears in the order requests were received, and it clears automatically -- you are emailed and the booking updates itself. Waitlists close 24 hours before departure.

Standby

Standby moves you to an earlier or later flight on the same day, at the airport, if a seat is free at the gate. It is not a waitlist and it is not free: same-day standby carries a flat charge, and it opens 24 hours before departure.
content_pages|booking-for-someone-else|s: Whose details go where, and who can then manage the booking.
content_pages|booking-for-someone-else|b:
Passenger details and contact details are different

Passenger names must match each traveller's passport exactly. The contact email and telephone can be yours, and that is where every notice about the flight is sent.

Who can manage it afterwards

Anyone holding the booking reference and the lead passenger's surname. There is no password on a booking, so treat the reference as you would a ticket.
content_pages|codeshare-explained|summar: What changes when the aircraft is not ours.
content_pages|codeshare-explained|body_h:
Reading the flight number

A flight sold under our number but flown by another airline is marked 'operated by' on the results page, on your itinerary and on the flight status page. The number you quote at the airport is the operating airline's, not ours.

What follows the operating airline

  • Baggage allowance, cabin service and seat pitch.
  • Online check-in, which must be done on their website, not ours.
  • Seat selection, which we cannot make on your behalf.

What stays with us

The fare rules, the refund, the change fee, and the miles you earn. Those follow the ticket, not the aircraft.
content_pages|checked-baggage-basics|sum: How allowances are structured. For your own route, use the allowance calculator.
content_pages|checked-baggage-basics|bod:
Pieces or weight

Two systems are in use and the route decides which. On a piece system you get a number of bags, each under a weight cap. On a weight system you get a total, and one bag may be heavier as long as the total holds. Mixing the two -- three bags on a weight route, say -- is what most excess charges come from.

What shifts the allowance

  • Cabin: Highland Class carries more than economy on every route.
  • Tier: silver and above add a piece or a weight bracket.
  • Passenger type: infants have their own small allowance plus a pushchair.

This page does not give your number

Allowances differ by route region, cabin and passenger type, so no figure printed here would be right for every reader. The allowance calculator asks for those three and returns the exact allowance for your journey.
content_pages|excess-baggage-charges|sum: The order the charges are applied in, and where each is cheaper.
content_pages|excess-baggage-charges|bod:
Three separate charges

  • Extra weight, charged per kilogram over your allowance.
  • An extra piece, charged as a flat fee per bag beyond your piece count.
  • An outsize or special item, charged at its own fixed fee, which replaces the per-kilogram rate rather than adding to it.

Prepaying is cheaper

Weight bought online before departure costs less per kilogram than weight paid at the bag drop, and a prepaid bundle costs less per kilogram than buying kilos one at a time. The airport rate is the highest of the three and is not negotiable.
content_pages|sports-baggage-quick|summa: A short summary. The full rules, with packing requirements, are on the special baggage page.
content_pages|sports-baggage-quick|body_:
The short version

Most sports equipment travels as one checked piece if it is inside your allowance and under the item's weight cap. Bulky items -- bicycles, surfboards, kayaks, windsurf rigs -- carry a fixed fee instead of the per-kilogram rate, and several must be declared before you travel.

What this page leaves out

It does not say how any item must be packed, which fee applies to which item, or which items we refuse. Those are on the special and sports baggage page, and the airport goes by that page rather than by this summary.
content_pages|delayed-baggage|title: If your bag does not arrive
content_pages|delayed-baggage|summary: What to do at the airport, and what we pay while a bag is missing.
content_pages|delayed-baggage|body_html:
Report it before you leave the airport

Go to the baggage desk in the arrivals hall and open a report. You are given a reference in the form PIR-100001. Reports opened after you leave the airport are accepted for 7 days but are harder to trace, because the bag has left our custody chain.

While it is missing

Away from home we reimburse essentials -- toiletries and a change of clothes -- up to USD 100 for the first 48 hours, against receipts. Most bags are located within three days. After 21 days a bag is declared lost and the claim moves to compensation.
content_pages|damaged-baggage|summary: The deadline, and the damage we do not cover.
content_pages|damaged-baggage|body_html:
Seven days

Report damage within 7 days of arrival, with the bag, the tag and the boarding pass. We repair where a repair is possible and pay the depreciated value where it is not. After 7 days we cannot accept the claim; this deadline is set by the carriage convention, not by us.

Not covered

Scuffs, scratches, dents and marks from ordinary handling; wheels, feet, handles and straps, which are wear items; overpacking that split a seam; and anything inside a bag that should not have been checked -- money, jewellery, electronics, documents, medication.
content_pages|baggage-on-connections|sum: When a bag is through-checked, and when you must collect it.
content_pages|baggage-on-connections|bod:
Through-checked

On a single booking your bag is tagged to your final destination and you do not see it in between, whichever airlines operate the legs.

When you must collect and recheck

  • Two separate bookings, even on the same airline and the same day.
  • A country that requires every arriving bag to clear customs, whatever your onward plan.
  • A change of terminal where the two are not connected airside.

Minimum connection time

We do not sell a connection shorter than the minimum for that airport, so a legal connection is long enough for the bag as well. If the first flight is late and the bag misses the second, it follows on the next service and we deliver it.
content_pages|valuables-and-fragile|summ: What must stay with you, and the limit of our liability.
content_pages|valuables-and-fragile|body:
Carry these yourself

Money, jewellery, precious metals, electronics, cameras, keys, passports and other documents, prescription medication, and anything irreplaceable. We accept no liability for these in checked baggage, whether the bag is lost, delayed or damaged.

Fragile items in the hold

A fragile item may be checked if it is packed for transport in a rigid case. It is tagged 'limited release', which means we carry it but do not cover damage to it. A fragile tag is not insurance.
content_pages|connecting-at-addis|summar: Minimum times, terminal moves, and what a long layover unlocks.
content_pages|connecting-at-addis|body_h:
Minimum connection time

60 minutes between two international flights, 90 minutes when one leg is domestic, and 120 minutes when the terminal changes. We do not sell a shorter connection, so anything you can book is long enough.

Long layovers

Between 8 and 72 hours on a single booking, a connection becomes a stopover: hotel, airport transfer, lounge and city tour options open up. Below 8 hours it is an ordinary connection and none of those apply.

Staying airside

If you do not leave the transit area you need no visa. The in-terminal hotel, the lounges and the prayer rooms are all airside. Leaving the airport means clearing immigration, and that needs a visa or an e-Visa.
content_pages|security-screening|summary: What comes out of the bag, and the liquid rule.
content_pages|security-screening|body_ht:
The liquid rule

Containers of up to 100 ml, all together in one transparent resealable bag of up to one litre, one bag per passenger. A 200 ml bottle that is half empty is still refused: the rule is the container size, not the amount inside it.

Exempt from the bag

Baby food and milk for a travelling infant, and prescription medication, in the quantity needed for the journey. Declare both at the checkpoint. Screening staff may ask you to open them.

Out of the bag

Laptops and tablets, the liquids bag, and coats. Shoes and belts only if asked. Duty free bought before a connection stays sealed in its tamper-evident bag with the receipt visible, or it will be taken at the next checkpoint.
content_pages|customs-and-duty-free|summ: Allowances on arrival, and what must be declared.
content_pages|customs-and-duty-free|body:
Declare on arrival

Currency above the local threshold, goods for sale, plant and animal products, and anything you were asked to carry for another person. Declaring costs nothing; failing to declare is what carries a penalty.

Duty free on a connection

Liquids bought airside travel in a sealed tamper-evident bag with the receipt inside. The seal must be intact at the next screening point. If your onward journey passes through a country that re-screens, buy on the last leg instead.
content_pages|weather-and-disruption|sum: What we owe you when a flight is disrupted, and what we do not.
content_pages|weather-and-disruption|bod:
Within our control

A technical fault, crew shortage or scheduling decision. We rebook you at no charge on the next available service, provide meals for a delay over 2 hours, and a hotel with transfers when an overnight stay is unavoidable.

Outside our control

Weather, volcanic ash, air traffic restrictions, airport closure, strike action by third parties, and security instructions from an authority. We still rebook you at no charge, and a refund remains available if you no longer wish to travel, but meals and accommodation are not provided.

Either way

Your checked bags travel on whichever flight you end up on, and a connection missed because of our delay is rebooked without a change fee.
content_pages|airport-arrival-times|titl: When to arrive at the airport
content_pages|airport-arrival-times|summ: Recommended times, and the three deadlines that actually bind.
content_pages|airport-arrival-times|body:
Recommended

Two hours before a domestic departure and three hours before an international one. Add an hour if you are checking sports equipment, travelling with an unaccompanied minor, or need a document check.

The deadlines

  • Check-in closes 2 hours before departure, online and at the desk alike.
  • Bag drop closes 60 minutes before departure.
  • The gate closes 20 minutes before departure, and a boarding pass does not hold it open.
content_pages|vaccinations|summary: Which certificates are checked, and who decides.
content_pages|vaccinations|body_html:
Yellow fever

A yellow fever certificate is required by many countries when you arrive from, or have transited, a country where the disease is present. It becomes valid 10 days after vaccination, so a certificate dated within 10 days of arrival is refused.

Who decides

The destination government, not us. We check that you hold what your destination requires, and we are obliged to refuse carriage if you do not -- but the requirement itself is theirs, and it changes. Confirm with the embassy before you travel.
content_pages|cabin-comfort-health|title: Staying comfortable on a long flight
content_pages|cabin-comfort-health|body_:
Why the cabin feels dry

Cabin air is pressurised to about 2,400 metres and its humidity sits near 15 per cent, well below a room on the ground. That is why skin, eyes and throat feel dry and why alcohol has a stronger effect than it does on the ground.

Circulation

Sitting still for hours slows blood flow in the legs. Walk the cabin roughly every two hours when the seatbelt sign is off, flex your ankles in the seat, and keep drinking water. If you have had recent surgery, a clotting disorder or a previous thrombosis, ask your doctor about compression stockings before you fly.
content_pages|travelling-with-medication: Where it goes, and the letter that prevents a problem.

Keep it in the cabin

Prescription medication travels in your cabin bag, in its original labelled packaging, in the quantity needed for the journey plus a few days. Hold baggage can be delayed, and the hold is cold.

The letter

Carry a doctor's letter naming the medication and the condition if you travel with injectables, controlled drugs, liquids above 100 ml, or a device such as a syringe driver. Some destinations restrict medicines that are ordinary elsewhere; check with the embassy rather than assuming.
content_pages|onboard-comfort|summary: Power, screens and amenities, and which aircraft have them.
content_pages|onboard-comfort|body_html:
Power

Wide-body aircraft have a universal socket and a USB port at every seat. Narrow-body aircraft have USB only. Turboprops have neither, so charge before you board.

Amenities

Highland Class on flights over six hours carries a flat bed, a duvet and an amenity kit. Economy on the same flights carries a blanket, a pillow and an eye mask on request.
content_pages|alcohol-and-water|summary: What is complimentary, and the limits on alcohol.
content_pages|alcohol-and-water|body_htm:
Complimentary

Water, tea, coffee and soft drinks on every flight. Beer and wine with a meal on flights over three hours. A full bar in Highland Class.

Limits

Cabin crew serve alcohol at their discretion and will stop serving a passenger who has had enough. You may not drink your own alcohol on board, including duty free. Both rules are safety requirements, not house policy.
content_pages|smoking-and-devices|summar: What is prohibited outright, and what flight mode covers.
content_pages|smoking-and-devices|body_h:
Smoking

Smoking is prohibited on every flight, in every cabin, including electronic cigarettes and heated tobacco. Lavatory smoke detectors are monitored and tampering with one is an offence in its own right.

Electronic cigarettes in baggage

Carry them in the cabin, never in the hold, and do not charge them on board. This is the same lithium-battery rule that applies to power banks.

Flight mode

Phones, tablets and laptops may be used in flight mode throughout. Larger devices are stowed for take-off and landing. Bluetooth headphones are permitted; a device that cannot be switched to flight mode must be off.
content_pages|miles-family-pooling|summa: Who can join a pool, and what pooling does not do.
content_pages|miles-family-pooling|body_:
The pool

Up to eight members of one household may pool. Every member keeps their own account and earns as usual; the pool is a shared balance that any nominated member may spend, and the pool head sets who may.

What it does not do

Pooled miles do not count towards anyone's tier. Qualifying miles stay with the member who flew, so pooling changes what you can spend and never what tier you reach.
content_pages|partner-earning|summary: How to credit a partner flight, and when it will not credit.
content_pages|partner-earning|body_html:
Quote the number when you book

Give your membership number at booking, not at the gate. A flight added afterwards credits within 6 to 8 weeks; one that never credits can be claimed for up to 6 months from the flight date, with the ticket number and the boarding pass.

Fares that earn nothing

Award tickets, staff and industry-discount tickets, tickets bought with a voucher for the full fare, and the deepest promotional fares on partner airlines. The fare rules on your booking say which applies.
content_pages|lounge-eligibility-explain: The four ways in, and what each one includes.

Four ways in

  • A Highland Class boarding pass for the flight you are about to take.
  • Gold or platinum tier, in any cabin, including one guest.
  • Silver tier, in any cabin, without a guest.
  • A walk-in pass bought for the visit, which anyone with a boarding pass may buy.

What entry includes

Buffet and bar, wi-fi, showers where the lounge has them, and a three-hour stay. Entry is at the departure airport only: a lounge at your destination is not part of your ticket, however you got into the one you left from.
